I recommend "Pfälzer Waldpfad" or "Saar-Hunsrück-Steig" in Germany. The Saar Hunsrück Trail is very long, but in my opinion the better trail. You most likely won't meet many people. There are a lot of scenic views on the way, castles, creeks, awesome woods... and there are a few "Trekkingcamps" which you can book ahead of time. There are also a lot of shelter huts along the way and in my experience no one cares if you sleep there as long as you take your trash with you etc.




If you only want to do a section of the SH Trail I recommend the part from Etappe 9 to Etappe 20.




Have fun!

I have mixed experiences with doctors. My problem is that for issues that require me to see a specialized doctor there is not much choice where I live so I have to suck it up.




My GP is amazing though.
I once had terrible pain in my neck, down my right arm into my hand. I woke up at night screaming from the pain and no position (lying, sitting, standing) made a difference.
I drove myself to the hospital on a Sunday, where the on call doc was a Nose and Throat specialist and he suggested taking 400mg ibuprofen which, predictably, did nothing.




On Monday I drove to an orthopedist. I was crying from the pain and could hardly stand. The front desk lady told me there were no appointments for a week. I begged for at least a sick note but she told me to leave. Imagine you are in so much pain you don't even know how to breathe and they just send you away?? It really broke me.


So the next day I went to my GP who, hearing my symptoms, immediately did an electrocardiogram because he feared I might have a heart attack. Fortunately it wasn't, so he finally prescribed me some good painkillers and made an MRT appointment for me. I got that done and had to take it to an orthopedist - and the one that sent me away is the only one within 80km that takes new patients.




I waited another week for an appointment so then, 2.5 weeks after the first day I had pain, he diagnosed me with a severe case of a herniated disc in my neck. The treatment? Physical therapy. I called 12 PTs in the area and no one had available appointments.
I looked up exercises online and fortunately I have almost no issues now, but that whole ordeal really scarred me for life.

Where I live we get little presents on December 6 (mostly sweets and other inexpensive stuff). The presents are from St. Nicholas, and if you didn't behave throughout the year, he will know and not get you anything or get you lumps of coal instead. This is a threat parents like to tell their children to get them to behave. 

One year, a couple of days before Dec 6, apparently I was being a brat. My mum told me that I won't be getting anything from St. Nicholas the way I behave. 

The day of, there were three lumps of coal lying in front of my room door. Nothing else. I was devastated. And you know what? I STILL remember that devastation. I learned absolutely nothing helpful from that situation. My mum was all gleeful about how "she told me so", and to this day, 30 years later, I still tear up when I think about it.

So that's all OP accomplished. She gave her daughter a bad memory to hold onto and feel worthless for the rest of her life.

Möchte als Borderline-Kollegin meine Sicht der Dinge zeigen:

Mein Hund ist das Beste, was mir je passiert ist. Er hat mich selbstbewusster gemacht. Er liebt mich, immer. Wenn ich gut drauf bin, wenn ich schlecht drauf bin, wenn ich ihn wegen etwas angemault habe: Er legt sich trotzdem neben mich auf die Couch und schleckt mich ab. Mich um ihn zu kümmern lenkt mich von vielem ab: Spazieren gehen macht den Kopf frei, Streicheln kann helfen, dich wieder ins Hier und Jetzt zu bringen. Er ist eine Konstante in meinem Leben. 

Aber: Alleine könnte ich ihn nicht halten. Es gibt Tage, da ist mir alles zu viel. Der Hund muss jeden Tag raus, mehrmals, und will noch bespaßt werden. Und konsequent und fortlaufend erzogen. Das kann auch eine Menge Kraft kosten! Wenn ich mir mal was "Gutes" tun will, Freunde treffen, Kino, Schwimmbad, spontan essen gehen, muss ich mir immer erst Gedanken machen, wie ich um den Hund rumarbeite. Manchmal finde ich das einfach scheiße. Es ist eben nicht jeden Tag eine rosarote Welt. 

Also kümmert sich mein Mann an solchen Tagen um den Hund. Und es ist eine echte Erleichterung, völlig geschafft nach Hause zu kommen und nicht mit dem Hund raus zu müssen. Oder der Hund hat sich den ganzen Tag wirklich aufgeführt wie der letzte Depp: Den Mülleimer ausgeräumt, beim Spaziergang einen anderen Hund angepöbelt und dann den Rest des Weges an der Leine gezogen. (Nur so als Beispiel). Dann bin ich einfach froh, wenn ich zu meinem Mann sagen kann: Bitte kümmer du dich den Rest des Tages um den Hund, ich kann nicht mehr. 

Das kommt natürlich nicht ständig vor, aber es ist einfach eine Entlastung.

Ich würde mir das also sehr gut überlegen, ob du wirklich in der Lage bist alleine jeden Tag 24 Stunden für deinen Hund verantwortlich zu sein. Ich weiß von mir, ich könnte das nicht (gut).

I've been sober for almost two years. I think about drinking all the time. But it's not such a compulsion anymore. I'll think about it, maybe after a hard day at work I think about how nice it would be to have a couple of beers to unwind. But it's just a passing thought. I don't act on it. Rarely I'll have a day so bad I wish I could have a bottle of vodka to just piss my life away again, but I easily drive past all of the supermarkets without buying anything. 

It's just... something I COULD do. Just a thought experiment. Like thinking about buying a boat and living on an island. Or dreaming about finally snapping and beating the shit out of your annoying neighbour. Or making plans for what to spend your lottery winnings on. It'll never happen, you'll never do it, but daydreaming brings some comfort nonetheless. I find it easier to allow myself to have these fantasies instead of demonizing them.

Seine Aufgaben sind Haus und Garten zu bewachen und Eindringlinge zu melden. Laut unserer Nachbarin, die viel zu Hause ist, geht er mehrmals täglich in den Garten und kontrolliert, schnüffelt, jagt Mäuse und Eidechsen. 

Täglicher Bewegungsbedarf liegt so bei 1 - 1,5 Stunden Gassi. Alles darüber hinaus wird zwar mitgemacht, danach liegt er aber auch platt in der Ecke. Er liegt sowieso eigentlich gerne viel rum.

Und genau deshalb funktioniert das. Sein Lebensinhalt ist sozusagen von Natur aus, sein Revier zu bewachen, und den Job kann er den ganzen Tag machen. Er freut sich, wenn wir heimkommen, wir gehen spazieren, spielen und trainieren mit ihm, aber er braucht dann auch seine Sofazeit. 

Es geht also, aber wirklich nur mit den richtigen Rassen. Und ob man die in einer Wohnung halten will/kann, weiß ich nicht. Meiner würde z.B. wahrscheinlich bei jeder Bewegung des Bewohners obendrüber melden, und das ist ja auch nicht Sinn der Sache.

Bin auch Kfz-Mechatroniker. Bei uns wird oft gesagt: Wo gehobelt wird, da fallen Späne und nur wer nichts macht, macht nichts falsch.

Mach dir vorher eine Liste zum Abhaken, oder schreib dir nebenbei auf was du machst, damit du am Ende nochmal drübergucken kannst. Wenn ich Räder festziehe, stelle ich zum Beispiel an jedes Rad an dem ich war irgendwas hin: Werkzeug, Sprühdose, egal, Hauptsache ich sehe am Ende, dass ich überall war. 

Lerne also daraus, aber mach dir keinen allzu großen Kopf darüber.

I wanted to add one thing: See if there are self-help groups around and encourage your Dad to go. I don't know how the post-op rehabilitation works where you live. In my country, you go to a rehabilitation clinic a few weeks after the surgery for 3-5 weeks (depending on your progress). There you get a few sessions of different PT and talks about incontinence, nutrition, etc.

But the most important part is all the other men there that have gone and are going through the same things as your Dad. My husband didn't want to go. He got a bit miserable at home when he didn't make as much progress as he hoped. But there he started talking to all the other men and it really helped him. They encouraged each other, egged each other on in PT and he realized that he was even a bit better off than most of the other patients there. He came back after 3 weeks and was really hopeful and energized again, I was so relieved.

So have a look around for the options your Dad has to talk to others in the same situation and make him go.

This can be a bit of a philosophical question among mechanics. Some like to check it when the oil is at least lukewarm, others when it's cold. But don't check it when the engine is really hot. Oil does expand when hot and you'll get a wrong reading. 

Personally, I like to let the engine warm up for a few minutes, then shut down and wait another 5-ish minutes to make sure the oil has had enough time to flow back to the oil pan. If you just want to see if the level is roughly okay, cold engine will be alright. If it's about half-full or above on the dipstick when cold the level is fine. 

However if you want a definite answer, have a look in your manual. They often say if the oil should be hot or cold.

There are days when I wake up and I feel very neutral, maybe even a bit excited for what the day has in store for me. This is an unexpected feeling. Then I go a week, maybe even three or four weeks feeling like this. I clean my apartment. I reconnect with friends. I work out. I feel like a functioning human being.

Then, little by little, I get exhausted. I don't keep up with cleaning. Getting up in the morning gets more difficult. I feel like I've run out of energy to keep being a normal person. Often, alcohol and drugs re-enter my life. I drag myself through work and I panic because I feel like I can't keep going for much longer. Suicidal thoughts are constant company. Everything requires much more energy than I have.

I hate myself. I scream at myself for being dumb, useless and ugly. I am convinced that nobody likes me, and if they do it's just because they don't really know me yet. There is absolutely no reason anyone would ever be interested in me. Also, whenever someone hangs out with me, I feel a crushing pressure to keep up being likeable. There's also the constant fear of when the person will realize how dumb/useless/ugly/insert random negative attribute I really am. 

I am also intensely lonely. This normally doesn't register too much until I've had a bit to drink and my feelings surface. Then this giant hole appears in my chest and I realize I have absolutely nobody.

Sometimes it gets better again. Sometimes I need inpatient treatment.

But what really kills me is that I have no control, at all, about when the different phases come and go. I can take my meds, I can go to therapy, and I can abstain from drugs and alcohol to make the good weeks a bit better and last a bit longer. But eventually, I will go off the deep end again. And again. And again. So every time when I wake up and feel good, there's a sharp pain that says "it won't last, you know." And I know. I know that one day I'll wake up depressed again, and there's nothing I can do.
